newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bourse opens higher, Rhone rockets.
newsitem.headline: French bourse opens higher, Rhone rockets.

text.p: French stocks ignored the U.S. dip overnight to notch up new highs on Thursday, as furious trading sent shares in drugs and chemicals group Rhone-Poulenc soaring on the back of news it planned to buy out U.S. subsidiary RPR.
Trading in Rhone shares was suspended briefly under price surge control regulations before trading started and the stock opened 15.15 percent higher at 244 francs a share.
It eased to 224.9 francs by 1028 GMT, up 10.85 percent, with a very heavy 3.1 million shares exchanged.
"There are huge orders coming in from everywhere. It's gone mad," said one trader.

The CAC-40 blue-chip index, which set a new clsoing record on Wednesday when it finished 2.97 percent higher at 2,867.44, edged ahead again on Thursday morning and stood 0.47 percent higher at 2,880.92 at 1030 GMT.
Computer services firm Cap Gemini suffered after its major shareholder, German industrial group Daimler-Benz, said it would sell its take in the French firm after six years in partnership.
The stock was down 5.71 percent at 325.3 francs at 1032 GMT.
CAC-40 volume 2.7 billion francs mid morning.
